verdict.rationale: Unleash's first-party docs cover environments that represent dev-to-production stages, each with its own flag configuration so a flag can be on in development and off in production. API tokens are scoped to a single environment: backend tokens are bound to one environment and one or more projects, and frontend tokens are documented separately. The Admin API also manages environments programmatically. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of environment isolation and environment-scoped keys.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage separate environments (dev/staging/prod) with independent flag states and scoped SDK keys

citations.quote: Environments represent different stages in your development lifecycle. They allow you to manage your product releases from local development to production.
each environment has different feature flag configurations. This allows you to enable a flag in development or test without enabling it in production.
Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
The Admin API provides full programmatic access to manage all resources within Unleash, including feature flags, projects, environments, users, and integrations.
